title: Agent Customizations may only extend inherited Core logic, never override it
content:
Each inherited Routine Protocol carries an Agent Customizations child (A.6.1.1.3.2.5.1.3.1.2.1.1, A.6.1.1.3.2.5.1.3.2.2.1.1, A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.2.1.1) with identical wording: the Agent "may define instance-specific customization of the routine protocol **to extend** the baseline functionality defined in the Sky Core Atlas. This can include custom routines or processes layered on top of the inherited Sky Core logic. Any extensions must remain fully aligned with the requirements specified in the Sky Core Atlas." Each currently reads "[No customization presently.]"

The verbs do the work. "Extend" and "layered on top of" describe additive composition; nothing in the slot permits replacing or disabling inherited behaviour. Combined with automatic upstream propagation, this makes the inheritance one-directional in both senses — the Agent cannot shadow the base class, and the base class can move under the Agent.

Providing an explicitly empty slot is itself useful. A reader can distinguish "this Instance runs pure Core logic" from "this Instance may have undocumented local practice," because the absence of customization is a positive statement in the Artifact rather than an inference from silence.

The design accepts an obvious limitation: an Agent that needs to *deviate* from Core logic — not merely add to it — has no route through this slot and must argue upstream instead.
description: Every Instance reserves a customization slot where a Prime Agent can layer routines on top of the Sky Core baseline, provided extensions stay fully aligned; Keel currently declares no customizations.
